requirements.description: Users must securely upload PDF documents with access control and encryption
System must extract text from PDF documents using OCR
System must detect and identify personally identifiable information (PII) within extracted text
System must store document metadata and PII findings in a queryable graph structure
Users must be able to query relationships between entities (documents, PII, metadata) via graph queries
System must enforce authentication and authorization for user access
System must provide audit logging and monitoring of document processing and access

Alert noise and false positives: suspicious activity detection requires careful tuning of alerting rules to avoid alert fatigue (too many false positives) while catching actual security events.

Add log integrity verification: implement audit log hashing (e.g., SHA-256 chaining) to detect tampering. Store hash chain in separate, immutable store.

blueprint.solution_summary: This AI document intelligence platform integrates secure PDF ingestion, OCR-based text extraction, PII detection, and graph-based entity relationship storage to enable compliance-ready document processing. Key decisions: REUSE HyperGraphDB for graph storage (mature graph-native architecture), REUSE OpenAM for centralized identity/access management (enterprise-grade IAM), ADAPT open-semantic-etl for OCR (strong capability match, requires API wrapper and error handling), ADAPT AEGIS for PII detection (purpose-built for PII with European compliance focus, requires accuracy validation and schema integration), ADAPT the knowledge-graph-from-LLMs project for graph querying (Neo4j backend maturity offset by non-deterministic LLM extraction to be replaced with deterministic COMP-003 output). The platform enforces end-to-end encryption, role-based access control, PII-aware audit logging, and graph traversal for entity relationship discovery. AWS deployment assumed for infrastructure (S3 for encrypted document storage, Cognito integration option for COMP-008, CloudWatch for observability integration with COMP-009).

risks: COMP-002 (OCR Extraction): open-semantic-etl project health unknown (no maintenance metrics provided). Risk of unmaintained codebase with unpatched security vulnerabilities. MITIGATION: Conduct GitHub verification (commit frequency, issue response rate), perform dependency security scanning before integration.

COMP-003 (PII Detection): AEGIS has no security audit evidence, maintenance status unknown, accuracy benchmarks not provided. False negatives expose sensitive data; false positives reduce usability. MITIGATION: Conduct security review, implement PII accuracy validation on representative dataset, establish baseline detection rates (precision, recall, F1).

COMP-004 (Graph Database): HyperGraphDB security posture unknown (no encryption at rest evidence, access control mechanisms undocumented), project health metrics unavailable, no PII-specific features. MITIGATION: Conduct security audit, implement application-level encryption layer, design custom access control wrapper in COMP-006, verify recent commits and project activity before adoption.

COMP-005 (Graph Query Engine): Reference implementation (CAND-020) is not production-ready; LLM-based extraction introduces non-determinism and hallucination risks not addressed by documentation. MITIGATION: Replace LLM extraction with deterministic COMP-003 results, conduct security audit on Neo4j deployment, implement comprehensive error handling and query validation.

COMP-006 (Orchestration - BUILD): Custom development increases engineering complexity and security surface area. Multi-component workflow integration creates many failure points. Integration bugs could cause data loss or security breaches. MITIGATION: Implement comprehensive unit/integration/end-to-end tests, conduct code security review (SAST), implement circuit breakers and fallback mechanisms, monitor error rates closely in production.

COMP-007 (UI - BUILD): Custom dashboard development introduces frontend security risks (XSS, CSRF, data leakage). Complex graph visualization (D3.js) may have performance issues with large datasets (10k+ nodes). MITIGATION: Implement security best practices (CSP headers, input sanitization, CSRF tokens), conduct frontend security testing (OWASP Top 10), implement pagination and virtualization for graph rendering, accessibility audit.

COMP-008 (OpenAM): No license confirmation provided; maintenance/security audit evidence missing. Centralized auth/authz point is single point of failure. MITIGATION: Verify license (likely CDDL or Apache 2.0), conduct security audit, implement OpenAM HA (high availability) with failover, regular security patching.

COMP-009 (Audit Logging - BUILD): Custom audit logging implementation must guarantee log integrity and immutability for compliance. Unauthorized access to audit logs could reveal PII and security events. Large log volumes (high-throughput document processing) require careful performance tuning. MITIGATION: Implement log encryption and tamper detection (hashing), role-based log access control, Kafka for reliable event streaming, Elasticsearch capacity planning.

Overall Architecture - Operational Complexity: System integrates 9 diverse components across ingestion, processing, storage, querying, security, and observability. Significant operational overhead for monitoring, maintenance, patching, and incident response. MITIGATION: Implement comprehensive documentation (runbooks, architecture docs, deployment guides), automated testing and CI/CD pipeline, centralized monitoring/alerting (COMP-009), incident response procedures, team training.

PII Data Handling - Compliance & Security: System processes sensitive PII data (SSNs, credit cards, health info) regulated by GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, etc. Data breaches could have severe legal/financial consequences. MITIGATION: Implement end-to-end encryption, role-based access control, comprehensive audit logging, regular security audits/penetration testing, compliance training, incident response plan.

Encryption Key Management: AES-256 encryption used throughout (COMP-001, COMP-004, COMP-009) requires secure key storage and rotation. Key compromise could expose all encrypted data. MITIGATION: Use AWS KMS or HSM for key storage, implement key rotation policies, audit key access, implement key usage monitoring.

Integration Testing Complexity: Multi-component workflow (upload→extract→detect_pii→store→query) requires comprehensive end-to-end tests. Missing test coverage could allow bugs to reach production. MITIGATION: Implement automated test suites (unit, integration, e2e), load testing, chaos testing, continuous testing in CI/CD pipeline.

Performance & Scalability: Async task queue (Celery) for high-volume document processing could become bottleneck. Graph queries on large PII datasets (millions of entities) could slow down. MITIGATION: Load testing to establish baselines, auto-scaling for Celery workers, database query optimization and indexing, caching strategies (Redis), monitoring and alerting for performance degradation.

Vendor Lock-in - AWS: Architecture assumes AWS deployment (S3, KMS, CloudWatch). Switching cloud providers would require significant rearchitecting. MITIGATION: Design abstraction layers for cloud-specific services (S3→object storage interface), document migration procedures, consider multi-cloud strategy if critical.

Third-Party Dependency Risk: System depends on open-source projects (open-semantic-etl, AEGIS, HyperGraphDB) which may have security vulnerabilities, maintenance gaps, or license changes. MITIGATION: Regular dependency vulnerability scanning (SBOM), automated patching, license compliance verification, maintain fork/backup of critical dependencies.

findings: Core architectural pattern (modular microservices with async task processing) is well-defined and consistent across components. Data flow from ingestion → processing → storage → retrieval follows logical separation of concerns.

Component responsibilities are clearly delineated, but integration points reveal coupling tensions: COMP-006 (orchestration) acts as central coordinator for all components, creating single point of orchestration logic. This is appropriate for workflow coordination but increases complexity if COMP-006 requires changes.

Security architecture is layered (encryption at COMP-001, auth at COMP-008, audit at COMP-009) which is sound in principle, but integration details create inconsistency: COMP-001 uses AES-256 for document encryption, COMP-004 requires separate application-level encryption layer (per decision notes), and COMP-009 implements log encryption independently. No unified encryption key management strategy documented across components.

Graph-based storage (COMP-004, COMP-005 separation) introduces architectural tension: COMP-004 stores graph relationships in HyperGraphDB but COMP-005 queries via Neo4j. Decision notes indicate Neo4j backend for graph querying, but stored data is in HyperGraphDB. This implies data synchronization, transformation, or dual-write complexity not explicitly addressed in architecture.

Role-based access control (COMP-008) is conceptually placed at identity layer but enforced at application layer (COMP-006) for document-level permissions. This distribution is reasonable but creates risk of enforcement inconsistency if authorization logic duplicated across components.

Async task processing (Celery) for document pipeline is well-justified but introduces eventual consistency model: intermediate results (extracted text, PII entities) may not be immediately queryable. Architecture does not explicitly document consistency guarantees or query staleness implications.

Technology stack mixing Python (FastAPI, Celery, open-semantic-etl, AEGIS), Java (HyperGraphDB), and potentially other languages (Neo4j queries) increases maintenance complexity but is justified by component-specific capabilities.

Missing explicit error handling architecture: decision notes mention 'error handling and retries with exponential backoff' and 'dead letter queue for unrecoverable failures,' but these are not formalized in architecture diagrams or component specifications. Failure propagation and recovery strategies need clarification.

Document processing pipeline data flow (upload → extract → detect_pii → store_graph) is clearly sequenced with explicit async task enqueue/dequeue pattern. Each step produces structured output consumed by next step.

PII entity data representation should be consistent across components but lacks explicit schema specification: COMP-002 extracts text, COMP-003 identifies entities (type, value, confidence, position), COMP-004 stores entities in graph, COMP-005 queries relationships. Schema definition for PII_Entity nodes not provided in blueprint—only referenced in implementation notes. Risk of impedance mismatch if component implementations diverge.

Encryption and decryption boundaries are implicit, not explicit: COMP-001 encrypts documents before S3 storage, COMP-002 must decrypt before OCR (decryption logic not shown in data flow), COMP-004 stores encrypted PII (encryption/decryption keys managed where?), COMP-009 stores encrypted logs. Data flow diagram does not show key retrieval/management flows.

Audit event data flow to COMP-009 uses Kafka (async, fire-and-forget pattern) which is appropriate for observability but creates timing gap: audit events are eventually consistent, not immediately queryable. Query on COMP-005 may complete before audit event is indexed in COMP-009. Architecture does not specify query-audit event ordering guarantees.

User authentication token (JWT) flows from COMP-008 through COMP-007 to COMP-006 API calls but intermediate processing (COMP-002, COMP-003, COMP-004, COMP-005) do not explicitly authenticate. Assumption is COMP-006 validates token and encodes user context in task metadata, but this is not documented in data flow.

Graph query results include PII entity values which require masking based on user role. Data flow shows masking occurs in COMP-006 before returning to COMP-007, but masking logic implementation (which values to mask, how to preserve query result integrity) is not detailed. Risk of inconsistent masking.

Real-time notification flow (WebSocket for task completion, dashboard metric updates) is mentioned in implementation notes but not detailed in data flow. Update frequency, payload structure, and consistency guarantees undefined.

Cache invalidation strategy for COMP-002 (extraction cache) and COMP-005 (query cache) is not specified. If cached results become stale due to PII detection result updates, refresh strategy not documented. Risk of users seeing outdated results.

Batch processing of PII detection results into graph storage (COMP-004) is mentioned but not detailed: are mutations transactional? Are partial batch failures handled? Can query results reference partially-ingested PII data? Consistency model unclear.

Data retention and deletion flows are not shown: COMP-009 audit log retention policy (1 year), GDPR delete requests, encrypted document lifecycle (when deleted?) not explicitly connected to component data flows.
Integration points are clearly enumerated (16 source-target pairs) with explicit purpose statements. Each component has defined inputs/outputs which is good foundational discipline.

API integration assumes REST endpoints (COMP-006 exposes /documents/upload, /documents/{id}/status, /queries/graph, /queries/{id}/results). GraphQL alternative mentioned but not designed. Consistency of API contracts (request/response schema, error codes, pagination) not specified.

COMP-002 ↔ COMP-006 integration uses Celery task queue but Celery result backend not specified (Redis, database, file system?). Large extraction results (100+ page PDFs) may not fit in Redis by default. Scaling implications not addressed.

COMP-003 integration assumes Python API (AEGIS wrapped in FastAPI service per decision notes) but REST call interface details missing: does COMP-003 accept raw text or pre-processed text? Does it return confidence scores? Format consistency unclear.

Assumption is COMP-006 writes to COMP-004 and COMP-005 reads from COMP-004, but separate database deployments create synchronization/consistency risk. Data replication strategy not specified.
